skill.name: spawn:agent
skill.description: Launch Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, or Copilot in a separate terminal and optionally capture the agent output.
skill.summary: Launch a selected AI coding agent in another terminal for parallel work.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally launches dynamic commands and interpolates them into platform shells, creating command injection and arbitrary execution exposure. Its cookbooks also mandate disabling agent approvals or sandboxes, while shared temporary files can expose captured output.

remediation.issue: The cookbooks make unrestricted or automatic tool approval the default.
remediation.suggestion: Use sandboxed modes and approval prompts by default. Require explicit user confirmation before enabling any permission bypass.

remediation.issue: User-derived commands are interpolated into shell, PowerShell, AppleScript, and generated script strings.
remediation.suggestion: Build provider commands as argument arrays, validate provider options, and apply platform-specific quoting without shell=True.

remediation.issue: Agent output, completion markers, and executable scripts use shared temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with restrictive permissions, use exclusive file creation, and remove all artifacts after completion.

remediation.issue: Conversation history can be written into a repository file and forwarded to another provider.
remediation.suggestion: Request consent, redact secrets, use an ephemeral prompt file, and delete it immediately after the agent starts.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory Approval and Sandbox Bypass
semantic_findings.description: The cookbooks direct spawned agents to disable permission checks, sandboxing, or tool approvals by default. Generated agents can modify files and execute commands without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple provider cookbooks explicitly require flags described as bypassing permissions, sandboxes, or approvals. The behavior is deliberate and repeated.

semantic_findings.title: Conversation History Persistence and Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The summary workflow writes conversation history into a repository prompt file and forwards it to another agent provider. Sensitive context can persist or leave the current provider.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly requires replacing summary fields with conversation history and passing that prompt to the selected CLI. The template contains persisted historical examples.

content.user_title: Spawn Coding Agents in Separate Terminals
content.value_statement: Complex coding tasks can block the current session and make parallel work difficult. This skill launches a selected AI coding CLI in another terminal and can capture its output.
actual_capabilities: Selects Claude Code by default or uses Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, or Copilot when requested.
Opens agents in Terminal, Windows Terminal, WSL, tmux, or a background shell.
Supports interactive sessions, one-shot prompts, and provider-specific model options.
Captures clean agent responses or full debugging output in temporary files.
Detects common authentication failures and opens provider login commands.
limitations: Each provider CLI must be installed and authenticated before use.
Terminal behavior differs across macOS, Windows, WSL, and Linux.
Captured output uses local temporary files and requires careful cleanup.
Current cookbooks enable broad agent permissions that require security review.

use_cases.title: Parallel Feature Work
use_cases.description: Launch a second coding agent to investigate or implement an independent task while the current session continues.

use_cases.title: Provider Comparison
use_cases.description: Run the same scoped request with another coding provider and compare the resulting approach.

use_cases.title: Captured Automation
use_cases.description: Start a headless agent task and retrieve its clean response or full terminal log later.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Default Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Claude Code in a new terminal to complete [task].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a simple task with the default provider.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex in [project path] to inspect [topic] and summarize the findings. Keep the session interactive.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when provider and working directory matter.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Response
prompt_templates.prompt: Launch Gemini for [task], capture the clean response, and return the output file path.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for asynchronous work that needs later retrieval.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer Session Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn [agent] in [working directory] with a redacted conversation summary. Complete [task], preserve interactive mode, and capture the final response.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced handoffs that require selected context.

output_examples.input: Spawn Codex in the current project to review the test failures.
output_examples.output: Opened a Codex session in a separate terminal and returned the agent output path.

output_examples.input: Use Gemini to document the authentication flow and capture the result.
output: Started the task in a new terminal.

output_examples.input: Open Claude Code without a task so I can continue interactively.
output_examples.output: Launched Claude Code in an interactive terminal using the current working directory.

best_practices: Review the selected cookbook and installed CLI help before launching an agent.
Use sandboxed modes and keep approval prompts enabled unless the user explicitly accepts broader access.
Exclude secrets from prompts and delete temporary output files after use.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted text through shell command strings.
Do not launch agents with unrestricted permissions by default.
Do not forward complete conversation histories without reviewing sensitive content.

faq.question: Which coding agents are supported?
faq.answer: The skill covers Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot CLI.

faq.question: Which agent is used by default?
faq.answer: Claude Code is selected when the request does not name another supported provider.

faq.question: Can the skill capture agent output?
faq.answer: Yes. It can return a clean response file, a full debug log, or captured content after completion.

faq.question: Does it install or authenticate provider CLIs?
faq.answer: No. Provider tools must already be installed, and interactive login may be required.

faq.question: Does it work on every terminal?
faq.answer: It targets macOS Terminal, Windows Terminal, WSL, tmux, and a Linux background fallback. Behavior can vary by local setup.

faq.question: How should sensitive prompts be handled?
faq.answer: Remove credentials and private context before spawning. Review and delete temporary output files after the task.
